programme.title: Handmade Wooden Spatula
programme.desc: The simple wooden spatula is an essential cooking tool that adds a handmade touch to any kitchen. George Vondriska demonstrates how to make your own wooden spatula in a few easy steps. This easy project makes a great gift for any home chef.

programme.title: End-Grain Cutting Board
programme.desc: Join George Vondriska to learn how to make your own end-grain cutting board that's sure to impress. Learn which types of wood work best for cutting boards and which materials to avoid when crafting anything that comes in contact with food. Find out how to properly glue, sand, and cut your pieces for a flat, even surface and achieve a finished product that is truly a cut above the rest.

programme.title: Accessorize
programme.desc: Every outfit needs the perfect accessory. This episode focuses on scarves and purses. Joanne Banko has four different seasonal scarves and ten tips. Then, Angela Wolf has a versatile envelope purse made from waxed canvas for any occasion.

programme.title: Off Our Needles
programme.desc: Hold onto your needles! Tracie and Jodi, are here to dish out fresh fiber inspiration. From project picks to wooly good gossip, things are about to get super knitty… and maybe just a little nutty.

programme.title: Perspective
programme.desc: Today's show is all about perspective or how we see objects in space. Perspective is the technique of representing three dimensional objects on a two dimensional space -- like drawing a house on a flat piece of paper. It's all a point of view from which we categorize or measure -- like a tree that gets smaller and smaller as we walk away from it. Our first example is an optical treasure box with geometric patterns. Next, build your own kaleidoscope. Add to your art journal -- how perspective makes buildings and other city scenes more realistic. Finally, make a lightweight ball with streamers and watch it fly through the air and learn about perspective.

programme.title: Texture
programme.desc: Today's show is all about texture -- texture is the feel or shape of a surface or thing. It's the smoothness or roughness, or maybe how soft or hard. We will learn about texture with a Paleolithic cave painting, a fun pony corral, and a friendly but prickly hedgehog. Learn how to add texture to your drawings with ordinary things from around the house in the Art Journal segment. Last, make a furry friend with giant chenille stems.

programme.title: Exotic Travels
programme.desc: Sometimes we get our sense of place right at home and other times our motivation comes from far off places and a sense of the exotic; something different from our every day. In this episode designers moved beyond their comfort zone. Up first Tracy Gonzales creates hamsa earrings featuring sari silk. Then Nealay Patel is back with earrings inspired by the exotic peacock. Finally, Tammy Honaman has tips for hiding fibers with an exotic and international flare when using a loom.

programme.title: Hammering, Torching and Shaping
programme.desc: Author and metal artist Mary Hettmansperger has some great ideas for hammering, texturing and coloring metal, plus using eyelets and rivets for cold connections. Katie's Beading Lesson is using snap finding to make jewelry quickly and easily.

programme.title: Episode 11: Die Cutting
programme.desc: Cutting has gotten very sophisticated – the newest tools allow us to do things we never thought possible. First, Jenny Barnett Rohrs demonstrates an inlaid die cutting technique to create card designs. Kazan Clark uses die cutting plus embossing to create straw toppers and more. Julie shares a last tip for transforming die cuts with a variety of techniques and tools, from doodles and stamps to markers and pens.

programme.title: Time Pieces
programme.desc: Time is measured in seconds, minutes and hours. This episode looks at ways to use those seconds better. First host Julie Fei Fan Balzer has a tip on using a timer. Then it's time for Joe Rotella and a perfect pendulum clock to keep track of time. Finally, Seth Apter has time saving techniques that are guaranteed to give you more time to create the art you love.

Modern quilter Riane Menardi combines hand quilting with machine quilting to create high-contrast designs with depth, texture and movement.

Finally, Cindy Hogan demonstrates the way the professionals cut machine embroidered designs for applique.

We finish with Angela Wolf and a lace trimmed tank. She will be featuring all different tank alterations from a basic pattern this season.

programme.title: Clay Workout
programme.desc: Stretch it out with clay. Polymer clay artist Syndee Holt creates a pendant with sparkle clay and adds an artistic touch with transfers and illustrations. To make a necklace, she recreates the Asian art of raku with clay and mica powders. Jewelry artist Anie Piliguian buffs clay elements to a sparkling finish.

programme.title: Episode 7: Mixed Media Techniques
programme.desc: Don't' be afraid to get a little bit messy. This show is all about mixing it up with mixed media. Kathy Cano-Murillo creates a color page with acrylic paint and water. Next, Julie demonstrates mono printing. Then Dina Wakley uses filmstrips, dyed cheesecloth and spray ink to create a page layout. Last, Julie uses office supplies and household items to create texture on her scrapbook pages.

programme.title: Folk Art

Jane Dunnewold shares another artistic perspective.

programme.title: Lines
programme.desc: A line is an infinitely extending one-dimensional figure; one that has length but not width or thickness. In art lines are the basis that give form to a piece of art. They can be straight or curved, thick or thin, and raised or flat. Projects featuring lines: a modern art canvas with paint and masking tape; lines become three dimensional as we make a playhouse for dolls or action figures; continue with your art journal and use brightly colored pens and a special tool to make spirograph line drawings. Finally make an unbreakable stained glass plaque with foil.

programme.title: Metal Stamping and Spiral Wire Wrapping

programme.title: DocFilm
programme.desc: There are few more polarizing figures in politics than US President Donald Trump. Admired and revered by his fans, criticized and literally condemned by many others, he's now in his second term of office.
programme.sub-title: Donald Trump - From Real Estate Mogul to US President

programme.title: Stepping Out
programme.desc: China is usually seen through the lens of economics, politics and a regimented population. But in Stepping Out we meet people who have left home and set out on the road to discover their China and themselves. Su Min, who feels she has done her duty as daughter, wife, mother and grandmother and in her 50’s left her abusive husband; Kiwi, a two-year-old whose parents lost their jobs in the pandemic and not owning a house, travel China in their RV as a family; and Alex a graphic designer exploring his country with his retired mother. Through their travels and their lives, we see a different life in China – a freedom to travel, explore, visit amazing places but taking all the benefits of technology to promote themselves and make a living. The film was made in July 2022 by students from CUC Nanjing and is directed by their tutor.

programme.title: Milan, Everyone At Home
programme.desc: It’s a hot Sunday in March in Milan, when Claudio Rizzotti, freelance filmmaker, decides to take his camera to document what is beginning to happen around him. It is the beginning of the Italian lockdown for the Covid 19 pandemic and so his city, his friends and his family sink into a long lethargy.

programme.title: The Great Awakening: QAnon
programme.desc: The far-right political movement known as QAnon has taken off around the world, mobilising a committed band of believers dedicated to fighting what they claim is an ‘online war’ against corrupt, child abusing elites. In the United States, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has declared QAnon a potential domestic terrorism threat. For one family, QAnon has caused division so severe that they had to report their relative - Tim Stewart, a QAnon conspiracy theorist - to Australia's national security hotline. In a concerning twist, it emerged that Stewart has had a longstanding friendship with Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison - leading to speculation about QAnon and Australia's highest ranks of political power. A look at the alarming movement which has caused ripples through the world, through the eyes of one family.

programme.title: Sheltered
programme.desc: In the busy world of the animal shelter, the loving bond between humans and animals is strained by the endless stream of abandoned cats, dogs, and rabbits. Pets are life companions - but for some, they are dispensable. With care and training by the passionate employees and dedicated volunteers, the hopeful animals are rehabilitated. Not every story has a happy ending, but the team fights on - even for the biggest misfits of them all.

programme.title: The Neutral Ground
programme.desc: In 2015, CJ Hunt was filming the New Orleans City Council’s vote to remove four confederate monuments from the city. A forceful group of critics protested the decision and fearing retaliation, no crew would agree to remove the statues. CJ sets out to understand why a losing army from 1865 still holds so much power in America. At once funny and furious, this film documents the USA's troubled romance with the Lost Cause.

programme.title: Man Up
programme.desc: Man Up! offers a critical look at the powerful role men can play in bringing about change within their homes and communities in order to lead more gender equitable and fulfilling lives. The film follows Sikhangele Mabulu and Monwabisi Mbetane as they reflect on their childhood socialization that has made violence an acceptable form of male expression.

programme.title: About the War
programme.desc: A reflection on war, on what the human being is capable of doing and on the job of reporter at the front. Fourteen years after recounting the conflict that shook Lebanon in 2006, Gianluca Grossi returns to the Land of the Cedars to confront a question that, over time,has become increasingly cumbersome: «What have I been used for? What is my job for? ».

programme.title: Greenwashing
programme.desc: It's a term that's come to the fore in recent years, as the urgency of the climate crisis becomes increasingly apparent. "Greenwashing" is a troubling phenomenon in which companies which brand themselves as 'sustainable' - in hopes of attracting green investment - continue to cause massive pollution. For the corporations responsible for a vast proportion of global emissions, just what lies behind the promises of climate action?

programme.title: Mr Fish: Cartooning From The Deep End
programme.desc: A personal documentary that follows a controversial political cartoonist as he struggles to provide for his family and stay true to his creativity in a world where biting satiric humor has an ever-diminishing commercial value.

programme.title: Where The Light Shines
programme.desc: Afghanistan's first ski team reach for a brighter future Where the Light ShinesFrom their amateur efforts at home in the Bamyan peaks, Sajjad and Alishah have the chance to ski for Afghanistan in the Winter Olympics. As local kids strap wood to their feet and imitate their heroes, the men face up to the difficulty of creating opportunities in a country that for generations has only seen war. Filmed over four years, this beautiful film paints an uplifting and refreshing portrait of Afghanistan as you haven't seen it before.

programme.title: Twisted Tales - The Butterfly
programme.desc: We uncover the hidden stories behind the butterfly'senchanting beauty. From their tough beginnings as caterpillars to the mysterious nocturnal lives of moths, discover how these creatures are more than just delicate beauties. Explore their fascinating transformation and cultural myths in this captivating episode.

programme.title: Discover China - The Emperor's Fantasy
programme.desc: Discover China is a documentary series shot in conjunction with the Chinese Ministry of Culture and China Central Television, including footage of never before seen locations and recreations of historical events. It was shot by BBC film crews over a four year period. At the foot of Tai Mountain sits an enigma, a temple that bears a striking resemblance to an Imperial palace. It was built by a brazen emperor, who ignored his country's desparation, and built this lavish shrine to bolster his status as the sole ruler.

programme.title: In the Starlight
programme.desc: In the Starlight is an intimate portrayal about the life of nature photographer Paul Zizka and his quest to capture the night skies.

programme.title: Immersion
programme.desc: The darkness, the muffled noises, holding your breath until the very last minute: this documentary plunges into the world of free diving. Lakes, rivers, oceans - the abyss is a source of fascination for Igor. Travelling from Switzerland to the world’s deepest blue hole in the Caribbean, Igor starts to compete and is crowned Swiss champion of free diving, descending to 82 metres.

programme.title: I Am Miriam Bin Laden
programme.desc: Mariam Bin Laden is going to swim across the English Channel. This represents not only an athletic challenge, but a symbolic and ardent dream: to give a second chance to her family, to inspire and empower Arab women to go after their dreams, as well as promote awareness for one of the most important issues of our time, refugees in dire need who are forced everyday to cross boundaries to survive.

programme.title: Mariupol: The Chronicles of Hell
programme.desc: Mariupol - ruined but not conquered. The city in the east of Ukraine has survived the occupation, total destruction, and a humanitarian catastrophe. The story of Mariupol is an especially horrifying one, with accounts reported that occupiers were murdering civilians, and actively preventing them from escaping. This film is the story of the survivors, and their life in a hell on Earth. Yet it's also a testament to the power of resilience, and Ukrainian fighting spirit.

It was shot by BBC film crews over a four year period. A much-celebrated ancient skull called the Peking Man was unearthed in Southwest Beijing in 1929 by Pei Wen Zhong, a young Chinese paleontologist.

programme.title: War Peace
programme.desc: War/Peace documentary film is re-introducing the radical student activists from the late 60s. Ex-leaders of The Weather Underground movement Bill Ayers and Bernardine Dohrn. For decades the government and press have tried their best to silence them. This film will serve as an historical reminder of what happened the last time a group of young minds planned to take over an unpopular government in Washington.

programme.title: A Gentleman Thief
programme.desc: Vincenzo Pipino is a thief, he was convicted and has done over 25 years in prison both in Italy and in the rest of Europe and has expiated his faults. The documentary tells the story of this last gentleman thief.

programme.title: Angel of Nanjing
programme.desc: The Yangtze River Bridge in Nanjing is the most popular place in the world to commit suicide, with over 5 attempts per week. For the past 11 years, blue-collar worker Chen Si has been patrolling this bridge every day, watching out for desperate people who've gone there to end their lives. With no formal training, he has saved over 300 people since he began; earning him the nickname the 'Angel of Nanjing'.

programme.title: We could be Heroes
programme.desc: Though Azzedine is a Paralympic champion, at home in Morocco, he is an outcast. Denied a salary or social care, even the right to train in the city stadium, Azzedine and his friend Yousef prepare for the next Paralympic Games in Rio, where they will be going for glory in the seated shot put. Returning from Rio after a golden performance, Azzedine hopes for a hero's welcome, but instead he must fight for his basic human rights.

programme.title: Discover China - Seeking the Peking Man

This film will serve as an historical reminder of what happened the last time a group of young minds planned to take over an unpopular government in Washington.

programme.title: A Gentleman Thief
programme.desc: Vincenzo Pipino is a thief, he was convicted and has done over 25 years in prison both in Italy and in the rest of Europe and has expiated his faults. The documentary tells the story of this last gentleman thief.

programme.title: Angel of Nanjing
programme.desc: The Yangtze River Bridge in Nanjing is the most popular place in the world to commit suicide, with over 5 attempts per week. For the past 11 years, blue-collar worker Chen Si has been patrolling this bridge every day, watching out for desperate people who've gone there to end their lives. With no formal training, he has saved over 300 people since he began; earning him the nickname the 'Angel of Nanjing'.

programme.title: We could be Heroes
programme.desc: Though Azzedine is a Paralympic champion, at home in Morocco, he is an outcast. Denied a salary or social care, even the right to train in the city stadium, Azzedine and his friend Yousef prepare for the next Paralympic Games in Rio, where they will be going for glory in the seated shot put. Returning from Rio after a golden performance, Azzedine hopes for a hero's welcome, but instead he must fight for his basic human rights.

programme.title: Discover China - Seeking the Peking Man

programme.title: Twisted Tales - The Wolf
programme.desc: We explore the terrifying myths and harsh realities surroundingwolves. Long feared as savage killers and vilified in stories from Little Red Riding Hood to Hollywood's werevolves, wolves are also respected in many cultures for their intelligence and social bonds. Discover the true nature of these misunderstood animals, their rold in the ecosystem.

programme.title: True or False
programme.desc: It is the most serious scandal ever hitting the modern art market. An affair that has made experts and auction houses tremble and has re-proposed the ghost of forgery. The facts date back to 2017 in Genoa, where an exhibition dedicated to the painter Amedeo Modigliani from Livorno was closed by the Public Prosecutor’s Office, which put 21 paintings out of the 60 on display under seizure.

programme.title: The Silent Scream
programme.desc: Since thirty years the data on the glaciers melting are truly alarming .There are men who have dedicated most of their lives to glaciers, photographing, measuring and monitoring them. This documentary collects their testimonies, bringing more awareness about the current state of glaciers and our mountains

programme.title: Unknown Distance
programme.desc: After five tours and ten years as a Marine Sniper, Sergeant Douglas Brown, alongside director and producer Gordon Clark, takes us on an emotional journey across America, documenting the powerful testimony of returning combat veterans - all trained with a deadly skill set, now rendered useless. How do these soldiers fit back into a society that supported them when they enlisted but became ambivalent when they returned?

programme.title: DIY Country
programme.desc: In Spring 2014, armed pro-Russian rebels stormed the city of Donetsk in eastern Ukraine. After seizing control of the city, the separatists held a referendum - labelled illegal by the US and EU - and independence from Kiev was declared. This brave documentary explores the origins and evolution of the Donetsk People's Republic, diving into hopeful beginnings and eventual descent into enduring conflict.

programme.title: Discover China - Taoism and Buddhism
programme.desc: Discover China is a documentary series shot in conjunction with the Chinese Ministry of Culture and China Central Television, including footage of never before seen locations and recreations of historical events. It was shot by BBC film crews over a four year period. Emei Mountain is a religious center for many sects of Chinese Buddhism. Long ago, it was the battleground where Buddhism clashed with one of China's leading religious at that time, Taoism.

programme.title: Russian Laundering
programme.desc: “Money mules” are people lured on the Internet and forced to launder money for hacker gangs and organized crime. Apparently serious jobs offers which become a nightmare. The documentary follows the money flow from Switzerland to Russia.

programme.title: Banzai Switzerland
programme.desc: Someone in Japan is in love with Switzerland, its culture, its folklore and, more specifically: the Swiss alphorn! The Tamagawa Alphorn Club from Nanasawa, Japan, is travelling to Switzerland to attend the International Alphorn Festival in Nendaz at the end of July. Alphorn playing started to be known in Japan in the 80ies and is becoming more and more popular in the last decade among retired people, but not only. Shigetoshi Nakagawa, founder of the group and a forest expert, is one of the first people who started to play the instrument; he has instructed to build and play the Alphorn in numerous regions, among children and elderly people. Thousands of Alphorn Clubs have been born lately and more and more Japanese are being interested in Swiss folklore culture and Switzerland in general.

programme.title: Origin of the Species
programme.desc: Abigail Child has been at the vanguard of experimental media since the 1980s. In her latest project, she offers viewers an eerie look into the present and future of AI, through the perspectives of scientists, entrepreneurs and a Black lesbian robot. Child’s thought-provoking film considers the emerging technology’s ethical and emotional implications, presenting a speculative, not-too-distant future grounded in sci-fi.

programme.title: Grit
programme.desc: When Dian was six she narrowly escaped a tsunami of boiling mud that completely submerged 16 villages under a moonscape of grit, leaving 60,000 people displaced. Lapindo, an Indonesian drilling company, had unleashed a violent, unstoppable flow from the earth's depths, estimated to continue for another decade. Shot over six years, GRIT witnesses Dian's transformation in to a politically active teen, as she and her mother take on the perpetrators.

programme.title: Twisted Tales - The Snake
programme.desc: We explore the complex and ften misunderstood world o snakes. Feared for their deadly venom and silent movements, snakes have also been revered as symbols of wisdom and health. This episode delves into the myths and realities of snakes, uncovering their fascinating behaviors, cultural significance, and the reaons behind our deep-seated fears.

programme.title: Kabul, Just Before Darkness
programme.desc: A Swiss Italian television crew was in Kabul in the days leading up to the surrender and was able to document the growing anguish of a society that feels the end of a hope cultivated for twenty years. Social, civil and democratic achievements, especially those made by women, are being swept away. It is also the starting point for a reflection on the fight against terrorism.

programme.title: Messages from the End of the World
programme.desc: The documentary describes the dramatic consequences of the climate change in the Arctic zone. Thanks to the Swiss Arctic Project five young people have been navigating for three weeks through hostile and beautiful landscapes up to the North. They have documented the signs of global warming and raise the new generation’s awareness through social networks.

programme.title: Echoes Of The Empire: Beyond Genghis
programme.desc: Mongolia: for most of us, it brings to mind Genghis Khan's mighty empire. But in the present day, there is also a rich culture in the nation that grew from the ashes of Genghis Khan's triumphs, and a complex history aside from the bloodshed and conquest. A stunning cinematic view of the country's past and present, from the remarkable evolution of the Mongol Empire to intimate portraits of today’s Mongolians.

programme.title: Where to Miss
programme.desc: In the sprawling, noisy madness of Delhi, Devki battles to achieve her dream - to become a taxi driver. The odds are stacked against her; the dangers, her sex and the deeply rooted traditions of Indian society. In this crafted and riveting doc we witness Devki's battle to accomplish her dreams. Within a city shaken by the bus rape of 2012, Devki strives to have the best that life can offer her. Her journey is anything but smooth.

programme.title: The Daily Dose
programme.desc: The Daily Dose is a highly personal documentary about the filmmaker’s struggle accepting lifelong antiretroviral treatment. Through the use of video diary entries; Skype conversations with friends and family; and experimental reflections, the film is a journey of self-discovery and affirmation.

programme.title: A Wing & A Prayer
programme.desc: The inspiring story of a pilot who overcame incredible odds to achieve his dream of flying solo across the Atlantic.

programme.title: 24 Hours At Gound Zero
programme.desc: An extraordinary inside look at the evolution of the World Trade Center horror, experienced through the eyes and the voices of people at the scene including a policeman, a fireman and an EMS worker who were among the first to arrive at ground zero. Our cameras wer the first on hand and we have some of the most definitive footage from the event of its time. This program aired on MSNBC.

programme.title: Peter Plan
programme.desc: Several years have passed since Peter decided to go and live in Plan, an isolated village at the Aragonese Pyrenees. Far away from the advantages of a city offers to a blind person, he survives through his art, rock music. Despite the recording of his latest album, daily life in this small village affects his mood and he is haunted by old memories. The seasons go on forever and each day the sheep bells toll louder. Something is about to go off in the Chistau valley.

programme.title: Unknown Distance
programme.desc: After five tours and ten years as a Marine Sniper, Sergeant Douglas Brown, alongside director and producer Gordon Clark, takes us on an emotional journey across America, documenting the powerful testimony of returning combat veterans - all trained with a deadly skill set, now rendered useless. How do these soldiers fit back into a society that supported them when they enlisted but became ambivalent when they returned?

programme.title: The Daily Dose
programme.desc: The Daily Dose is a highly personal documentary about the filmmaker’s struggle accepting lifelong antiretroviral treatment. Through the use of video diary entries; Skype conversations with friends and family; and experimental reflections, the film is a journey of self-discovery and affirmation.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: Discover China is a documentary series shot in conjunction with the Chinese Ministry of Culture and China Central Television, including footage of never before seen locations and recreations of historical events. It was shot by BBC film crews over a four year period. A much-celebrated ancient skull called the Peking Man was unearthed in Southwest Beijing in 1929 by Pei Wen Zhong, a young Chinese paleontologist.

programme.title: A Wing & A Prayer
programme.desc: The inspiring story of a pilot who overcame incredible odds to achieve his dream of flying solo across the Atlantic.

programme.title: 24 Hours At Gound Zero
programme.desc: An extraordinary inside look at the evolution of the World Trade Center horror, experienced through the eyes and the voices of people at the scene including a policeman, a fireman and an EMS worker who were among the first to arrive at ground zero. Our cameras wer the first on hand and we have some of the most definitive footage from the event of its time. This program aired on MSNBC.

programme.title: Man Up
programme.desc: Man Up! offers a critical look at the powerful role men can play in bringing about change within their homes and communities in order to lead more gender equitable and fulfilling lives. The film follows Sikhangele Mabulu and Monwabisi Mbetane as they reflect on their childhood socialization that has made violence an acceptable form of male expression.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: Discover China is a documentary series shot in conjunction with the Chinese Ministry of Culture and China Central Television, including footage of never before seen locations and recreations of historical events. It was shot by BBC film crews over a four year period. At the foot of Tai Mountain sits an enigma, a temple that bears a striking resemblance to an Imperial palace. It was built by a brazen emperor, who ignored his country's desparation, and built this lavish shrine to bolster his status as the sole ruler.

programme.title: True or False
programme.desc: It is the most serious scandal ever hitting the modern art market. An affair that has made experts and auction houses tremble and has re-proposed the ghost of forgery. The facts date back to 2017 in Genoa, where an exhibition dedicated to the painter Amedeo Modigliani from Livorno was closed by the Public Prosecutor’s Office, which put 21 paintings out of the 60 on display under seizure.

programme.title: The Curse of The Terracotta Warriors
programme.desc: The Curse of the Terracotta Warriors tells the little known story of the seven farmers who in 1974 uncovered the Terracotta Army of China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang, and how their lives were forever changed after their discovery.

programme.title: Mr Fish: Cartooning From The Deep End
programme.desc: A personal documentary that follows a controversial political cartoonist as he struggles to provide for his family and stay true to his creativity in a world where biting satiric humor has an ever-diminishing commercial value.

programme.title: We could be Heroes
programme.desc: Though Azzedine is a Paralympic champion, at home in Morocco, he is an outcast. Denied a salary or social care, even the right to train in the city stadium, Azzedine and his friend Yousef prepare for the next Paralympic Games in Rio, where they will be going for glory in the seated shot put. Returning from Rio after a golden performance, Azzedine hopes for a hero's welcome, but instead he must fight for his basic human rights.

programme.title: Sorojchi
programme.desc: "Sorojchi" is how altitude sickness is known in Bolivia and it is something that is felt in the cities of El Alto and La Paz. It is here where we learn the story of four urban artists who, through their work, share their views on Bolivia and Bolivians, immersed in a big social and political crisis.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: No one could have dreamed that from this baby boy, born to a noble family on a financial and social decline, would grow one of China's most influential, iconic and important historical figures. From his early days, mimicking the religious rituals, to a young man who traveled throughout China, advising kings and emperors on how to rule, the man ultimately became a living legend, as his teachings and his memory are still revered and worshipped to this day in modern China. Discover China follows in the footsteps of one of China's most important cultural heroes, Confucius.

programme.title: Frontline Fashion
programme.desc: Frontline Fashion is an award-winning docu-series that follows the most talented emerging fashion designers from all over the globe

programme.title: Built Different
programme.desc: 12-year-old Paige Calendine was born bilateral without legs.Paige has never let her disability hold her back, in fact just the opposite. She is a very successful athlete, who competes against kids who are not disabled, and wins! She even qualified for the state tournament in two sports: gymnastics and archery. The documentary is going to showcase her talent. Her inordinate determinational and courage make her Built Different.

programme.title: The Mundo King
programme.desc: If you dream it, they will come. This cosmic exploration paints the portrait of artist Rolf Schulf's pursuit to make is dreams come true through his engless toil to complete he majestic Mundo King Castle on a hill in the Dominican Republic.

programme.title: Who Made You?
programme.desc: Artificial intellignce is reaching our mental and physical existence like never before. The film leads us to the world of cyborgs, sex robots and androids. It challenges us to face our values, ethics and rethink our position. To keep our humanistic values on board with the development, we have to be awake - tight now. Eye-opening scences from Finland, Spain, Swedenm Geece amd Japan reveals the on-going processes and development on a global level. The guide in our stimulating journey is a young aspiring Dr Michael Laakasuo who is making pioneering research on the field of ethics and AI. He stresses that machine-ethics should not be left behind in the technological development. The film asks what the development of AI means to us as human beings. What does it mean for humanity, community, and how it will affect our perception of human? What are the values we want to hold on to?

programme.title: Circuits of Care
programme.desc: By 2036, one in three people in Japan will be over the age of 65. While the nation wrestles with a shrinking labour force, the Robot Revolution Initiative was launched to expand robotics into every corner of Japanese economy and society. Circuits of Care follows anthropologist David Prendergast as he meets researchers developing and testing assistive technologies for older adults. From cybernetic walking supports to companion robots and automated sensor networks in nursing homes, older adults and care professionals share their experiences of the practical benefits these technologies bring, the problems they create and the unexpected relationships that can blossom.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: At the turn of the century, a Child-Emperor ascended to the throne of the Chinese Qing Dynasty. Emperor Pu-Yi’s Reign was short lived and mired with treason, corruption and external influences. After abdicating his throne, Pu Yi knew his days in the imperial palace were numbered. Questions of his survival as a commoner began to trouble his mind. Upon looking at the wealth of priceless artifacts collected over 500 years of imperial reign, Pu Yi began plotting ways to smuggle these riches out. However, Pu Yi was not alone. Discover China brings you the story of how the precious treasures of the Imperial City disappeared from the capital palace, and where some reside today.

programme.title: Frontline Fashion
programme.desc: Frontline Fashion is an award-winning docu-series that follows the most talented emerging fashion designers from all over the globe

programme.title: Haunted New Orleans
programme.desc: In the heart of the Big Easy, restless spirits reveal chilling tales-voodoo curses, spectral jazz, and forgotten secrets. Ghosts, cryptids, and eerie history explore the supernatural secrets of New Orleans in this chilling documentary.

programme.title: Nothing Is Left But Our Tenderness
programme.desc: A forgotten bridge, a house in ruins, a remembered melody: for many, the armed conflict in Peru at the end of the 20th century has changed the country. The Andes has become a mirror reflecting a fragmented memory that is difficult to reconcile. Nothing is left but our tenderness accompanies men and women who confront the traces left along the way.

programme.title: Drag Invasion
programme.desc: In 2017, dozens of drag queens from the international reality competition RuPaul's Drag Race arrived in Lima and sold out at each of their presentations. This is the chronicle of an unsuspected phenomenon that mobilized and empowered the LGBTQ + community, in a country that is still extremely conservative, religious and homophobic.

From cybernetic walking supports to companion robots and automated sensor networks in nursing homes, older adults and care professionals share their experiences of the practical benefits these technologies bring, the problems they create and the unexpected relationships that can blossom.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: At the turn of the century, a Child-Emperor ascended to the throne of the Chinese Qing Dynasty. Emperor Pu-Yi’s Reign was short lived and mired with treason, corruption and external influences. After abdicating his throne, Pu Yi knew his days in the imperial palace were numbered. Questions of his survival as a commoner began to trouble his mind. Upon looking at the wealth of priceless artifacts collected over 500 years of imperial reign, Pu Yi began plotting ways to smuggle these riches out. However, Pu Yi was not alone. Discover China brings you the story of how the precious treasures of the Imperial City disappeared from the capital palace, and where some reside today.

programme.title: Frontline Fashion
programme.desc: Frontline Fashion is an award-winning docu-series that follows the most talented emerging fashion designers from all over the globe

programme.title: Haunted New Orleans
programme.desc: In the heart of the Big Easy, restless spirits reveal chilling tales-voodoo curses, spectral jazz, and forgotten secrets. Ghosts, cryptids, and eerie history explore the supernatural secrets of New Orleans in this chilling documentary.

programme.title: Nothing Is Left But Our Tenderness
programme.desc: A forgotten bridge, a house in ruins, a remembered melody: for many, the armed conflict in Peru at the end of the 20th century has changed the country. The Andes has become a mirror reflecting a fragmented memory that is difficult to reconcile. Nothing is left but our tenderness accompanies men and women who confront the traces left along the way.

programme.title: Drag Invasion
programme.desc: In 2017, dozens of drag queens from the international reality competition RuPaul's Drag Race arrived in Lima and sold out at each of their presentations. This is the chronicle of an unsuspected phenomenon that mobilized and empowered the LGBTQ + community, in a country that is still extremely conservative, religious and homophobic.

programme.desc: A wrong choice leads to a dilemma

programme.title: Road Trip Masters
programme.desc: Brian and Nick road trip to Havre de Grace, a waterfront town on the banks of the Susquehanna River. They sample the best of creole cuisine, get hands on in the decoy business and experience the Bay!

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: The remains of an animal skull at JiuZhaiGou Valley in northern Sichuan Province brought about a change in mindset, proving at long last that this lush, green valley was indeed home to one of China's greatest national natural emblems – The Giant Panda. With their food supply in sharp decline, natural calamities that threaten their very existence and with a little help from human intervention, these gentle, docile giants were nearly extinct from this magical valley. However, due to some fortunate involvement by the local government, the population of this magnificent animal is finally managing to survive. Discover China as we follow the footsteps of Dong Ga – The Panda.

programme.title: Serbia: Old and New
programme.desc: Having explored Serbia's capital city, Laura Alexandra travels into the countryside in pursuit of an old Roman trail. Her journey will take her back and forth through 1 million years of history.

programme.title: Royal India
programme.desc: Samira visits a 300 year old fort and meets a young royal who rolls up his shirt sleeves and cooks a classic hunting dishpart of a magnificent multi course dinner.

programme.title: Our New Zealand Escape
programme.desc: Justin and Nicole Marshall experience the best that Marlborough has to offer and Nicole overcomes a major fear in the process.

programme.title: Escape To Paradise
programme.desc: The Caribbean has always been a dream destination for holidaymakers dreaming of that perfect getaway, and Antigua has long been a favourite for the British. Of course, it spent several centuries under British rule, and the connections endure in names such as Nelson’s Dockyard and English Harbour. Today though, it’s the 365 beaches, year round sunshine, and colourful cocktails that bring the visitors.

programme.title: Ellen's American Adventure
programme.desc: It’s the final leg of the journey for Ellen’s adventure. After experiencing Space City Houston it’s onto the coastal city of Galveston to visit the seaside and uncover it’s secrets.

programme.title: Aqua Challenge
programme.desc: High stakes! Diving without a mask, surrounded by sharp reefs!

programme.title: Road Trip Masters
programme.desc: The guys check into a luxurious estate near La Grange then check out how some of the world’s finest bourbon is made, meet some incredible horse ladies and tour a famous baseball factory.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: In a slumbering village nestled in southeast China’s huizhou district in Anhui province, sits a mysterious hall. The village’s empty streets reveal the ancestral pride and worship that have been taking place for generations, to this very day. The village’s residents, in their unique, picturesque houses, lead a peaceful and harmonious existence, unfettered by the troubles of the world. Yet the origins of this quiet, pastoral village belie an age old story of imperial intrigue and incredible perseverance, as generations living in the village continue to commemorate their ancestors. Discover China follows the path of the mystery of the Hu Clan.

programme.title: A Wing & A Prayer
programme.desc: Mark Oremland had a a dream - to fly a DC-3 from England to Nerw Zealand, recreting the famous 1936 flight by Jean Bastten - the first person to fly that route.

programme.title: Royal India
programme.desc: Samira play spolo on the Royal polo fields, and visits Mehrangarh fort, a place Rudyard Kipling described as “Built of Angels and Giants”.

programme.title: Our New Zealand Escape
programme.desc: Petra Bagust and Hamish Wilson travel to Rotorua for an energetic weekend break and raft down the world’s largest commercial waterfall.

Yet the origins of this quiet, pastoral village belie an age old story of imperial intrigue and incredible perseverance, as generations living in the village continue to commemorate their ancestors. Discover China follows the path of the mystery of the Hu Clan.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: In the west, seeking the land of Shangri-La has long been a lost cause. In China, a similar story, written by a fourth century poet drove countless scholars, poets, writers and painters in pursuit of this magical utopia. This work of fiction, however, seemed to have its roots in the real world, as numerous locations around Southern China bear striking resemblance to the poet’s descriptive words. In the west, over one thousand years after the poet’s story was published, a novel with remarkable similarities introduced the concept of Shangri-La to the world. Discover China, as we set out on a unique journey, seeking the Land of Peach Blossoms.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: In the west, seeking the land of Shangri-La has long been a lost cause. In China, a similar story, written by a fourth century poet drove countless scholars, poets, writers and painters in pursuit of this magical utopia. This work of fiction, however, seemed to have its roots in the real world, as numerous locations around Southern China bear striking resemblance to the poet’s descriptive words. In the west, over one thousand years after the poet’s story was published, a novel with remarkable similarities introduced the concept of Shangri-La to the world. Discover China, as we set out on a unique journey, seeking the Land of Peach Blossoms.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: A plethora of caves, caverns and grottoes, once served as the Chinese Nation’s gauge of political and religious stability. The sands of time are lifted to tell the tale of ancient nomadic tribes and their dominion over this land, near the city of Datong in Shanxi Province. The tribe leaders likeness’ etched for eternity onto the statues in the rocky caves symbolizing their once savage and absolute reign over China’s northwestern regions. Additionally, sing the praises for the clan’s leaders as they flourished and evolved into one of China’s earliest imperial dynasties. Discover China opens the door to the mysterious world of the Yungang Grottoes.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join Ellen Coughlan as she explores the iconic city of New Orleans. Nicknamed the “Big Easy”, it’s known for its round the clock nightlife, vibrant live-music scene, and a spicy, singular cuisine… reflecting its history as a melting pot of French, African and American cultures. New Orleans is famous for its Mardi Gras, where parades and street parties fill the city. It’s also home to the iconic Natchez Steamboat, the last completely steam powered paddleboat on the Mississippi River.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: When Diana got engaged, she was constantly in the media's eyes. Throughout her life, she focused on her sons and committed herself to charity work, like speaking out against land mines. Diana used her fame to bring attention to this and other important issues. This well-researched show takes a closer look at one of the 20th century's most amazing people. With never-before-seen footage, it shows her path from a shy teen to becoming the beloved Diana, Princess of Wales, including touching moments from her last days.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: Saskatchewan’s bitter cold and unforgiving wind makes for brutal days and nights for Chris and Casey. A rainstorm adds more difficulty and discomfort. Mentally drained and hungry, the brothers must try new tactics to find food and warmth.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: The lack of hunting opportunities have drained Chris and Casey’s patience. Arguments ensue when they disagree over staying put, or portaging to a new lake. Signs of a bear remind the brothers that they must remain focused in order to stay alive.

programme.title: El Desprecio

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: The practice of hiring private armies goes back to ancient times, and the mystique associated with the mercenary warrior has been the subject of many historical studies and fictional characterizations. This episode of CQB takes a more contemporary look at a day in the life of a group of civilian contractors, and how their role has evolved on the modern battlefield. Using its “sub-second” analysis techniques and intimate first-person footage, CQB reveals the backgrounds, training and equipment of today’s “soldiers for hire” and how private armies are re-shaping the way conflicts are conducted around the world.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: In this classic western, Clint Eastwood - aka "Blondie" - saves Eli Wallach from the hangman's noose three separate times by shooting and severing the rope that he hangs from. We recreate each scene and test the reality of these shots with the weapons that were used.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: John McLain (Bruce Willis) finds himself dangling from the side of a building. The only way to save himself is to shoot through the glass window and break through to safety. Using the same Beretta 92 handgun, we reconstruct the office glass and see if our host can break through.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: With still no big game in sight, Chris and Casey are forced to rely on fishing for food. The cold temperatures have slowed down the fish, creating challenges. When Mother Nature brings a brutal snow storm, the brothers are tested likenever before.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: In this episode on Wardens, we're on the hunt for a troublesome bear that's been rummaging through the neighborhood garbage. Meanwhile, in another area, we're giving citations to a bunch of folks for fishing without a license.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: Tanalian Aviation battles winter weather to ferry ice climbers onto the Knik Glacier.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: From the elite ex-special forces personnel in charge of guarding heads of state in conflict zones to the two-person teams that protect CEOs in dangerous regions, modern day bodyguards must be well versed in close quarter battle techniques. An immense amount of planning and preparation is involved in each operation. From air travel, car convoys and helicopter shuttles to basic foot traffic, a close protection squad must be completely tuned to the Who, What, Where and When of any given situation. This episode of CQB focuses on the complex day-to-day and minute-to-minute operations of these elite teams and the highly developed techniques they employ.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: John Rambo's ability to decimate enemies all by himself has created some of the most incredible weapon stunts in Hollywood history. We test the reality surrounding these iconic scenes from this blockbuster franchise.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: Can you really fire a GE Minigun handheld with ammunition held in a backpack (also seen on Predator (1987). Additionally, for one of our larger tests - can you actually chop down a jungle forest with a Minigun? Actor Bill Duke - who co-starred with Arnold Schwarzenegger for the film and who's character performed this weapon stunt - joins us to find out. But first, we have to build a jungle.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: Papua New Guinea Pt2. Jim brings meat to the local village while Corey explores leech infested swamps looking for the local deer. Local villagers tell Jim of a remote area 400 miles away where buffalo roam.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: After weeks of trying to survive in Saskatchewan, Chris and Casey have yet to kill big game. Time is running out as the bear begin to hibernate. Mental willpower is wearing thin. But a message from back home changes everything.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: A turn of events lifts the brothers’ spirits, but creates a huge hurdle they must overcome as they enter a new race against the clock.Chris and Casey reflect on the challenges they have faced so far, and the challenges that still lie ahead.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: Montana Game Wardens are keeping an eye out for people breaking hunting laws, like trespassing, hunting too early, hunting from cars, or taking spike elk.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: Tanalian Aviation pilots Joel Natwick and Josiah Freeman assist with a search and rescue for an experienced hiker deep in the winter wilderness.

programme.title: El Desprecio
programme.desc: Following the September 11 attacks, military presence became commonplace in New York and other American cities, and the counter terrorism forces were effectively given a “blank cheque” when it came to ensuring that another terrorist incident would never take place on American soil. This episode of CQB takes an in–depth look at who was selected to occupy elite anti-terrorist positions, what they were trained for, and how they were equipped: when opposing forces are using commercial airliners and chemical weapons, countermeasures are by necessity complicated and varied. CQB takes an intimate look at what it was like to be an officer on alert for chemical attacks in Washington DC, or an army reservist monitoring suspicious activities on the streets of NYC.
